name: WE_SHC_3671375
description: Wurth Elektronik WE-SHC two-piece board-level shielding cabinet, COVER part 3671375 -- candidate Faraday-tier EMI shield over the gate-drive / high-di/dt switching-node area (TODO.md 7.1). This build (Faraday EMI tier) uses it per docs/decision-matrix.xlsx EMI Hardening sheet.
verification: MECHANICAL / NO-SCHEMATIC-SIGNAL PART -- a shielding can has no functional electrical pins; it is placed and sized on the PCB layout (frame soldered to the board's shield-ground pour) and represented here purely as a schematic placeholder with one 'shield-to-ground bond' reference pin so it can be dropped on a sheet and net-tied to GND. Dimensions confirmed directly from the local copy of [19] (WE order code 3671375, rev. ViM 002.000, 2025-05-12): inner 29.5mm x 37.7mm, outer 30.1mm x 38.3mm, height 3.8mm ref. -- matches prior secondary-sourced figures. CORRECTION found in the local datasheet: 3671375 is the COVER ONLY ('Assembly with Frame: Frame (3670375), Cover (3671375)') -- it is not a complete shield by itself and MUST be paired with the WE-SHC Frame, part 3670375. UPDATE 2026-08-02: the frame's own local datasheet has since been added and verified -- see symbols/specs/WE_SHC_3670375.json and REFERENCES.md [30]; this BOM gap is now closed at the datasheet level (still needs a matching symbols/WE_SHC_3670375.kicad_sym instance placed alongside this cover in the actual schematic, and a BOM line added). The local datasheet is a 5-page mechanical/packaging spec only -- it does NOT contain the 60dB/500MHz-3GHz shielding-effectiveness figure cited from secondary sources in REFERENCES.md [19]; that figure remains secondary-sourced pending a shielding-effectiveness test report (neither the cover's nor the frame's datasheet states it). See TODO.md 7.1-7.2 and 12.1. BOARD STATUS RESOLVED 2026-08-15: the cover gets NO footprint and is marked 'exclude from board' in the build schematic, while remaining in the BOM. Its datasheet has no Recommended Land Pattern sheet at all -- because nothing about it is soldered; it clips onto the FRAME (3670375), which is the piece that carries the land. Inventing a land pattern for it would be a fabricated design decision under AGENTS.md Sec.1.3. Same treatment as BT1-BT6, the off-board 21700 cells.
